Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can line up the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

Summary from our side:
- ML/infra context: you run an in-house recommendation reranker that will call a 4k-context instruction-tuned model for reranking and short summaries.
- Traffic profile: expected steady-state ~100 requests/sec during peak windows, spiking to ~220 RPS for 15–30m during promotions.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end for the model call needs to be <= 90ms for the customer-facing flow (tight SLA ask).
- Data controls: no regulated PII requirement today; procurement will confirm whether we need a VPC later.

Clarifying Qs so we can recommend a pragmatic next step:
1) Can you confirm the 100 RPS sustained number is for concurrent single-token-ish prompts or for multi-step flows (multiple model calls per user)?
2) Any absolute blackout dates for procurement/PO? You mentioned an April funding window — is that when you need terms finalized?
3) Are you open to a short Dedicated POC if Hosted can't hit the p95 target?

Recommended immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Aditya to share quick perf thresholds and a few benchmark datapoints for similar workloads.
- If Hosted is close to target, run a 2-week pilot on Hosted with throttles and cache rules; otherwise, we propose a 7–14 day Dedicated POC on reserved capacity (non-production) to validate p95 and throughput.

Please confirm the answers to 1–3 and we can schedule the POC window ASAP.

Thanks,

Jordan —

Thanks for the details. A few concrete datapoints and suggestions to help you evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated:

Perf baselines (approximate, for a 4k-context instruction-tuned model; numbers are token-generation p95 server-side only):
- Hosted (multi-tenant, dynamic infra): p95 ~ 110–160 ms at 100 RPS for short outputs (<=128 tokens) depending on model variant and region. We do automatic batching and KV caching, but multitenancy and burst isolation cause higher p95 at sustained 100 RPS in some profiles.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool - single tenant): p95 ~ 40–70 ms at 100 RPS for the same model on a 1–2 node A100 configuration with tuned kernels + continuous batching; Dedicated scales predictably with added nodes for throughput.

Key tradeoffs for your stated constraints (100 RPS steady, 90ms p95 target):
- If you must guarantee p95 <= 90ms under sustained 100 RPS, Dedicated is the safer choice. Dedicated gives predictable latency SLOs and isolation; we can reserve capacity to meet the SLA and run a smoke test to verify.
- Hosted may be able to meet p95 during non-busy regional windows or with short outputs + aggressive prefix caching, but it is less deterministic for sustained high RPS bursts. Hosted offers faster time-to-value and lower upfront cost.

Security/compliance notes:
- Hosted supports IP allowlisting and per-request audit logs (retention configurable; default 30 days). Logs are tenant-scoped but aggregated in our control plane — if your security policy requires customer-controlled logging or HSM-backed keys, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the option.

Cost ballpark (very rough):
- Hosted: estimated $0.0008–$0.0022 per token (depends on model), for your workload we estimate $15k–$40k/month (token usage dependent).
- Dedicated: committed monthly capacity (example): $65k/month for a 2xA100 reserved pool with autoscale headroom (lower per-token unit cost at higher commit and predictable monthly spend).

Attachments: I'm attaching a short perf smoke report from a similar retail reranking workload so you have a concrete datapoint. It includes raw latency histograms and the config used.

Suggested next steps:
- If you want to validate Dedicated: we can provision a non-prod Dedicated pool for a 7-day POC (we'll need a short SOW and an internal procurement ticket).
- If you'd prefer to try Hosted first: we can run a 2-week pilot with config constraints and increased observability (token traces + p95 alerts) — we should also set a go/no-go gate at day 5.

I'll attach perf-smoke-202703.pdf and link our Hosted vs Dedicated benchmarks. Happy to jump on a short call with your infra/security folks if helpful.

Best,
